articleTitle: Bones detection in the pelvic area on the basis of YOLO neural network
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article focuses on application of You Only Look Once (YOLO) neural network in the process of individual bones recognition, in the set of CT slices of human pelvic area. The network was trained on custom data and then it was employed to detect bone structures in similar yet different CT data. The accuracy of the detection was investigated. In the final step, the bounding boxes of detected regions, created by the YOLO algorithm were employed to position the idealized models of bones with respect to CT data.

articleTitle: Analysis of Facial Features for the Use of Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents a face image classification system for emotion recognition. In the first step skin recognition, using the elliptical boundary model, is performed. Then, the detection of facial features takes place. Next, an algorithm for extracting geometric and anthropometric features, from the face image is activated. Finally, training and testing classifiers are performed. We achieved averaged classification accuracy 57.7% for 6 different emotions (joy, surprise, sadness, anger, fear and disgust) and average accuracy 95.9% for 2 emotions (joy and surprise).

articleTitle: Specific Absorption Rate Evaluation in Human Body Model Comprising of Metallic Implant
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, the human body absorption of electromagnetic energy emitted by a dipole antenna operating at the current mobile phone technology frequencies is investigated. The specific absorption rate within a realistic anatomical model comprising of the metallic implant was evaluated. The research was carried out using electromagnetic numerical modeling based on the Finite Integration method. The primary objective was to compare levels of absorbed electromagnetic energy as a function of the antenna distance and mobile phone carrier frequency. The effect of implants presence was also studied. The results show that SAR varies with respect to the antenna distance as well as to the considered mobile phone technology standard. However, the antenna shift in the tens of millimeters provides significant SAR decrease below the safety limit. The presence of metallic implant in superficial tissue layers causes significant SAR increase, particularly for PM implant while the SAR enhancement for needle implant was negligible.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of a Transformer with Differential Electromagnetic Parameters
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The mathematical model of a transformer with differential electromagnetic parameters is proposed. To calculate these parameters, the magnetic system of the transformer is approximated by a planar circuit with a single magnetic flux (without splitting it into the main flux and the leakage flux). The parameters of the elements of this circuit are determined on the basis of geometric dimensions and the main magnetization curve of magnetic core material.

articleTitle: Automatic Identification of Drill Condition During Drilling Process in Standard Laminated Chipboard with the Use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to the identification of the state of drill wear and tear during the drilling process. Identification provides for three states (classes) of drill which were marked according to traffic lights classification: red - “useless” (worn out), yellow (still sharp but should be manually assessed by a specialist), green -“useful” (sharp). Red state indicates symptoms of drill worn out and determines that it should not be used during the drilling process (does not satisfy the furniture process quality). Yellow drill state should draw attention to the fact that the drill may be excessively blunt. Later on, it is recommended to assess the drill manually. When the system indicates the green state of drill, it means that the drill may still be used in the drilling process, maintaining the high quality of drill holes. The recognition of drill state is based on 5 registered signals: feed force, cutting torque, noise, vibration and acoustic emission. The hardest part in the implementation of automatic identification of drill condition is to find appropriate features, which will separate cases belonging to 3 classes (states). When input data are presented in the form of images, we can use the convolution neural network, but in that case we have signals registered as time series, hence the long-short term memory (LSTM) is applied.

articleTitle: Matrix Equation of L.A. Zadeh and its Application to the Analysis of the LPTV Circuits
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The equation L. A. Zadeh presented in the matrix form, which is applied to the construction of the frequency symbolic model of the LPTV circuit in the frequency domain. Such a matrix model is divided into several independent matrix equations, the number of which is equal to the number in the range of signal sources. The matrix equation is proposed to be solved by the frequency symbolic method, which involves the symbolic solution of a system of linear algebraic equations. Comparison of time spent on solving such systems by standard MATLAB and d-trees methods. The latter has shown its undoubted advantage. An example is considered.

articleTitle: Methods of Power-Band Extraction Techniques for BCI Classification
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The purpose of the article is to check whether the method of estimating EEG signal energy, treated as a feature, has an impact on the classification accuracy in BCI systems. The experiments were carried out on EEG signals recorded during the imagination of left or right hand movement. For energy estimation in 8-12Hz band, the following methods were used: variance, autoregressive model, discrete Fourier transform, and mutual correlation. The usefulness of the features was checked using the 10-CV test and the LDA and QDA classifiers. The results indicate that the best average classification accuracy was obtained for bandpass filtering and the energy estimation method with the use of variance.

articleTitle: Proof of Concept EMG-Controlled Prosthetic Hand System - An Overview
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: This article discusses the design of a proof of concept (POC) system for preliminary control of a prosthetic hand based on EMG signal processing. Included is the description of signal processing steps, an overview of the constructed prosthetic hand prototype and preliminary interfacing thereof with the control interface. Further development will include prerecorded EMG signal processing and classification of various hand movements using neural networks, with the ultimate aim of designing a system capable of real-time signal classification in order to control the prosthetic hand when worn by a person.

articleTitle: Shape and Topology Optimization of High Power Converter Busbar
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The paper is divided into two parts. In the first section the paper deals with shape optimization of high-power converter busbar. The second section is focused on the topology optimization which was applied on the busbar. The main goal of the optimization is to ensure that the power is equally distributed among particular active components.

articleTitle: Control and Supervision System for Micro Biogas Plant
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents the concept of a micro biogas plant control system. For the needs of a specific installation, an electrical installation design and a control system based on the PLC controller and a HMI SCADA visualization system has been made. The selected techniques were reviewed and their technological aspects were characterized. The conditions of anaerobic fermentation in the bioreactor were analyzed. The required technical and technological criteria for the production of biogas were indicated.

articleTitle: Calculating Power Losses In LV Cables Loaded With Nonsinusoidal Currents
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: Harmonic currents in power cables cause additional power losses associated with phenomena that increase the temperature of the cable insulation and make its service life shorter. For these reasons, it is important to choose methods for determining active power losses, which ensure adequate computational accuracy. This paper compares the methods for determining active power losses on the example of a low voltage cable line supplying a non-linear load.

articleTitle: Information Technology for Electrophysiological Approach of Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Identification During Surgery on Neck Organs
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: Information technology for electrophysiological approach of recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) identification during surgery on neck organs is considered in the paper. This technology consists of 4 main steps: obtaining of information signal as result of stimulation of surgery wound tissues; segmentation of information signal; selecting of the main spectral component of segments of information signal; modeling of distribution of the main spectral component amplitudes for RLN identification. A mathematical model for RLN identification is considered as an interval discrete model that is, the difference scheme. Efficiency of proposed information technology is shown.

articleTitle: Prerequisite for HRV biofeedback: Real-Time Detection of R peaks
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects the physical health and ability of the organism to handle stress situations. HRV biofeedback is a real-time training process which helps reduce stress and asthma severity. The most important prerequisite for the HRV biofeedback is the detection of R peaks in the ECG signal. This article describes in detail a real-time algorithm capable of R peaks detection. The algorithm is implemented within a standalone C# application and functionality thereof is demonstrated. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm is immune against various types of artefacts.

articleTitle: Automatic recognition of the kidney in CT images
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents an original method of kidney recognition in CT images. Fast and precise visualization of a kidney is a very important task in medical diagnosis of kidney cancer. Calculation of a precise kidney's boundary allows to visualize any changes in the genitourinary system requiring specialist intervention. The method presented in this article uses shape analysis of objects' boundary and calculates geometrical coefficients for final detection. The results of the experiments show that the level of accuracy of automatic kidney boundary detection is 84 % comparing to expert's results.

articleTitle: Simple Polynomial Method for Inductance Calculation in Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: This paper describes development of a simple method for phase inductance calculation of a switched reluctance motor. The proposed method can provide inductance values with comparable accuracy to look-up table approach, but with much lower demands on system memory which can enable usage of a lower cost micro-controller unit.

articleTitle: Stability of Interval Positive of Integer and Fractional Orders Continuous-Time Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: Theasymptotic stability of interval positive of integer and fractional orders of continuous-time linear systems is investigated. The classical Kharitonov theorem is extended to the interval positive of integer and fractional orders continuous-time linear systems. It is shown that: 1) The interval positive linear systems is asymptotically stable if and only if the matrices A1, A2 are Hurwitz Metzler. 2) The interval positive fractional systems are asymptotically stable if and only if A1, A2 are Hurwitz Metzler. 3) The interval positive of integer and fractional orders continuous-time linear systems with interval characteristic polynomials are asymptotically stable if and only if their lower bounds of the coefficients are positive.

articleTitle: DC Charger Simulation Results Compared to Measurements
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents Matlab Simulink simulation model of an electric vehicle charger. The results of the simulations are compared to the results of measurements registered in the actual distribution network supplying the DC charger, showing good agreement.

articleTitle: Testing of electrical signals from piezoelectric sensors in application for counting grains in seeding machine
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article discusses the use of piezoelectric sensors to control the movement of grain in agricultural seed machines. The piezoelectric sensor model and laboratory stand has been used for this study. Next the grading accuracy tests were carried at this stand for two seed species of the selected speed and for two sowing standards. Also selected suitable materials for optimum durability of the sensor. Grain counts are made using the ME-RedLab PMD-1208LS measuring module connected via USB to a PC. This module has a 16-bit counter used to count beans. A special computer program was used to support this module, using features included in the Red Lab software.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Priority Queueing Systems Using Timed Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The following article presents research results and performance analysis of Priority Queuing System (PQS) that are supporting the Quality of Service (QoS). Priority queuing models supporting three traffic classes (high, medium and low priority) in 5-3-1 architecture were designed and tested. The performance assessment of the tested system was carried out using temporal Petri nets. The use of simulation tools in the form of Petri Nets (PN) allowed for the evaluation and verification of waiting times, queuing mechanisms and traffic intensity using the queuing algorithm. It was shown that temporal models of Petri nets can be effectively used in modeling and analysis of the performance of priority queuing systems.

articleTitle: Data Mining of Electricity Consumption in Small Power Region
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The aim of the paper is mining the electricity consumption data in a small region of Poland. The unsupervised and supervised methods have been applied, including K-means, KNN and neural networks. Chosen factors characterizing profiles of power consumption related to different seasons of the year and different types of the day (working versus non-working) have been considered. The numerical experiments performed on the real data of small power region have shown interesting relationships which are useful in prediction of the future need of the power. The prediction results for the 24-hour load pattern for the next day have shown superiority of neural network application.

articleTitle: Active Contour Method for Segmentation of the Glands in Colon Histology Images
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The needs of modern medical diagnostics increasingly set new research directions and allow to improve current technologies. Gland segmentation is an important step on the way to automate the diagnosis of pathogenic changes in the colon. Without rapid and correct diagnosis it is not possible to take appropriate treatment. A small number of specialists, long education of future experts and widening from year to year the number of specialized probe commissioned cause significant lengthening of waiting for results and negatively affect the quality of the research. In this work we developed and presented gland segmentation algorithm can automate the most time consuming elements of the diagnostic process.

articleTitle: Adaptation of the Artificial Mains Network (AMN) to the Updated Requirements of CISPR 16-1-2:2014
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: This paper presents analysis of operation of the processes occurring as a result of artificial mains network (AMN) modification. Methods of construction changes of AMN will be considered, which are aimed at meeting the requirements included in the requirements of CISPR. This article also covers the results of measurements that will confirm the correctness of the modifications made, among others impedance measurement between each terminal of the power cord and the housing for one- and three-phase sockets, measurement of the voltage division factor by the direct method and the isolation factor.

articleTitle: Biomaterial Crack Geometry Estimation Using Eddy Current Inverse Approach
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The main subject of this paper is inverse problem approach to non-destructive evaluation of conductive austenitic stainless steel as biomaterials. Eddy current evaluation under harmonic excitation is used. Magneto-resistive effect sensors are there in the role of pick-up elements. Basic cracks geometry is inversely estimated based on computational algorithms. The gained results are presented and discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Derivative Differential, Inductive Sensors for Short Magnetic Pulse Measurements
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents the proposal solution of the magnetic field sensor design process. The task aims at design the low cost, “single use” inductive coil capable of the measurement rapid high level electromagnetic pulses in destructive conditions. The measurement environment makes it impossible to use reference sensor for its vulnerability and price. Proposed sensors are verified against reference Montena B-dot SGM2G sensor. The results of the 4/16μs standard shock impulse measurements together with additional simulations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Diffraction of the Plane Waves by a Strip with PEC-Impedance Boundary Conditions on its Faces
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: A direct collocation technique is applied in modeling and simulation for scattering from a strip with PEC-impedance boundary conditions. By using the Green theorem the mixed boundary value problem is reduced to a system of hypersingular integral equations. Numerical results of scattering fields characteristics are presented.

articleTitle: Detecting symptoms of driver fatigue using video analysis
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: medical image processing; medical signal processing; prosthetics; computerised tomography; production engineering computing; eddy currents; pulse measurement; feature extraction; mathematics computing; finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Assessment of Specific Absorption Rate in Human Torso Model Comprising of Metallic Implant Near Short-Wave Diathermy Applicator
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: In this paper, the human body absorption of electromagnetic energy emitted by a short-wave diathermy applicator is investigated. The specific absorption rate within a layered human torso model comprising of pacemaker implant was investigated. The research was carried out using electromagnetic numerical modeling based on the Finite Integration method. The primary objective was to compare levels of absorbed electromagnetic energy as a function of diathermy applicator distance. The effect of implants presence was also studied. The results show that SAR varies with respect to the applicator distance from the human torso. However, the applicator shift in the tens of centimeters provides significant SAR decrease. The distance of 50 cm between the applicator and human torso model was identified as the so-called safe distance which is consistent with published measurement outcomes.

articleTitle: An Improved Solution for the Skin and Proximity Effects in a Tubular Screen
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The paper describes an analytical method for eddy currents induced in tubular conductors of a system of two parallel tubular conductors by a transverse alternating magnetic field generated by a current in one of them. The skin effect is taken into consideration. The magnetic field is presented by means of a vector magnetic potential as Fourier series. The proposed solution can be used to describe semi-analytically the current density induced due to the proximity effect in high current bus ducts or gas insulated lines (GILs) with tubular conductors. Therefore, the extent of its potential applications is wide, and the considered problem has a practical significance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Eddy Current System using Equivalent Multi-Branch Foster Circuit and Edge Element Method
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The paper deals with the synthesis of the equivalent model of the systems with an electromagnetic field, using the Foster Circuit (FC). The way of determining the lumped parameters of the FC of the considered system, using a time-harmonic field model, has been discussed. In order to develop the field model, the edge element method (EEM) has been applied. Moreover, the way of determining the lumped parameters of the FC has been illustrated on the example of the studied system, consisting of a solenoid coil and a conductive core. The obtained results of the calculations have been compared with the results, using the transient field model of the phenomena of the considered system.

articleTitle: Analytical-Numerical Solution for the Proximity Effect in a Tubular Screen
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The aim of this paper constitutes analysis of eddy currents induced in a system of two parallel tubular conductors by a transverse alternating magnetic field generated by a current in one of them. The magnetic field is expressed via vector magnetic potential as Fourier series. Using the Laplace and Helmholtz equations as well as the classical boundary conditions we determine analytically the current density induced due to the proximity effect. Though the paper is theoretical, nevertheless high current bus ducts or gas insulated lines (GILs) with tubular conductors are universally used. Therefore, the extent of potential applications is wide. So the considered problem has a practical significance.

articleTitle: Interval arithmetic, hull-consistency enforcing and algorithmic differentiation using a template-based package
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The paper presents the first author's C++ library ADHC for algorithmic differentiation and hull consistency enforcing using interval calculus. The code is based on C++ templates, so that the same source code could be used to generate binary functions for various cases: for evaluating the function value, its various derivatives or creating expression tree to enforce hull consistency. Also, we can choose at compile-time to use sparse or dense containers for higher derivatives. Preliminary experiments are reported.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Platform of AC-DC Converters Components
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The paper presents application of two selected algorithms for an online platform for multicriteria optimization of AC/DC converters. The purpose of the platform is to speed up selection of components to satisfy the four main objectives in power electronic circuits: total power loses, weight, volume and total price. The system generates a pareto front for the objectives considering several constraints. It uses a discrete optimization scheme searching the database of available components. The database of components contains magnetic elements, semiconductors and capacitors used in a few typical configurations of AC-DC converters. The paper focuses on presenting a concept of the system which allows to put together simulators of different components calculating objectives with modern multicriteria optimization algorithms (NSGAIII, SPEA2). The system proved to be very effective even for large databases of components composed of tens of thousands of items.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Approaches to Implementing Measured Hemodynamic Parameters within an Electromechanical Analogy-based Human Body Arterial Model
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The objective of this study was to explore the possibility of combining the theoretical human arterial model based on electromechanical analogy with real impedance cardiography measurements - the fusion of which would create a per-person adaptable model. Cardiac activity was modeled based on two different sources - the first model (Model No.1) included real-life hemodynamic parameters based on variation of universal aortic pressure, while the second model (Model No.2) was based on real-life aortic flow derived from measurements. Simulated blood pressure propagation in proximal aortic segment was compared with reference pressure values measured by an electronic sphygmomanometer. Model No. 2 was found to be more accurate and better representative of real behavior of the arterial system under normal conditions. Additionally, the blood pressure and blood flow curves directly reflected the variability of the cardiac activity.

articleTitle: Error Estimation of the Nonlinear Systems Simulation Using Convolution Integral
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The present paper explores the error estimation for piecewise approximation of nonlinear systems using convolution integral. The base for the proposed method is the relationship between convolution integral and z-transform. The problem of error estimation is simplified using complete system decomposition to two elementary dynamic blocks - integral (zero pole) and first-order (one real pole). For each block, possible cases of changes in their parameters are considered- one parameter in the integration block and up to two parameters in the first-order block. Theoretical principles confirmed by computer simulation using the simple model also been presented.

articleTitle: The Analogous Human Arm Circulatory Model of Artificial Anastomosis
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The aim of this research is to design a computational model for study purposes of the pressure and flow waves in a human upper limb with dialysis vascular access. Model is based on electromechanical analogy. Human hand contains arteries and corresponding veins arches. Radio-cephalic wrist arterio-venous fistulae (AVF) are a preferred choice to other types of vascular access for haemodialysis. In these models we can study the effect of arterial - venous anastomosis on blood pressure wave propagation in arterial and venous region.

articleTitle: Verification of Adapting Fixtures for Noncoaxial Devices Measurements
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: Measurements of noncoaxial devices are influenced with adapting fixtures that allow embedding them in a test setup with coaxial ports (like measurements with Vector Network Analyzer). CISPR-16-1-4 defines rules of thumbs for such adapting fixtures to ensure TEM wave propagation in such transmission lines. In this paper we verify the correctness of the rules on the basis of computer simulations and highlight the impact of adapting fixtures on measured impedance.

articleTitle: Tests and Analysis of Loop Type Long-Flashover Arrester
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: This paper presents analysis of operation of the loop type long-flashover arrester (LFA) working as overvoltage protection of medium voltage overhead lines with covered conductors. In this research the LFA was tested in the laboratory with standard lightning impulse voltages. The resulted sparks were registered with fast camera and the results were compared with spark development predicted with numerical simulations. This paper also presents developed relation between breakdown voltage of loop type long-flashover arrester and the arrester distance to power line wire. That relationship helps to coordinate insulation level of both LFA and insulation of protected line.

articleTitle: Mobile Sensor Network for Suspended Particulate Matter Measurements using Kriging Interpolation
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: In this paper a project of low-cost mobile sensor network for evaluation of air quality in metropolitan areas is presented. Data processing in this system is addressed with the kriging interpolation. For this purpose a specialized software framework was implemented and used to execute numerous simulations of such system as if deployed on a scale of large city. Simulations are complemented with proposal for low-cost realization of mobile sensor network based on public transport vehicles. It is also shown how a slight trade-off in temporal-spatial resolution effectively improves final outcome of the interpolation provided that network nodes take advantage of mobility feature. Results from numerical experiments are used to evaluate quality of kriging technique applied to mobile and hybrid sensor networks.

articleTitle: Induction Heating-Assisted Laser Welding of Stainless Cylindrical Pipes
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: A 3D model of induction-assisted laser welding of stainless cylindrical pipes is presented, incorporating two physical fields: magnetic field and temperature field in the welded pipe that influence one another. The model is solved in quasi-coupled formulation using software COMSOL Multiphysics 5.3.

articleTitle: Simulation of U-shaped Eddy-Current Converter of Transformer Type for Defective Monitoring in Ferromagnetic Samples
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The results of theoretical researches of construction of a eddy-current defectoscope with a coupled measuring oscillatory circuit with a transformer coupling for the quality monitoring of welding seams of metal products are presented. This device can be used in eddy-current (electromagnetic) defectoscopy for automatic and manual control of metal products in cases where it is difficult to fix the gap between the laying-in eddy-current converter (inductance coil), which contains the measuring oscillatory circuit, and the controlled surface of the ferromagnetic product. The main advantages of using coupling oscillatory circuits in the construction of resonance eddy-current defectoscopes are presented.

articleTitle: CO2 Absorber Condition Monitoring in Closed-Loop Respiration Devices
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The presented article deals with the topic of monitoring CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>absorption in a closed loop diving apparatus. While partial pressure is monitored in the closed-circuit breathing loop using oxygen sensors, carbon dioxide is not monitored at all. However, higher carbon dioxide or oxygen content in the breathing medium has toxic effects on the organism. CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>absorber composition, manufacturing thereof and chemical reactions occurring during CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>absorption are discussed - based on this a device for monitoring the exothermic absorber chemical reaction is constructed. The proposed device estimates the time to CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>absorber depletion based on the displacement of the chemical reaction zone.

articleTitle: Anatomy-Aware Spinal Cord Stimulation in Magnetotherapeutical Applications
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The presented article details anatomy-aware spinal cord stimulation based on patient-specific spinal cord coordinates computed from computer tomography data. Digital image processing methods and algorithms are used to extract spatial points representing the spinal cord canal and are subsequently used to precisely guide the electromagnetic applicator (e.g. figure-of-eight coil) along the patient back so as to focus the electromagnetic energy within the spinal cord canal and minimize surrounding tissue exposure. A comparison between manually (e.g. physician, doctor) and computer guided applicator is presented based on numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Anthropometric facial features in emotion recognition
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: An article presents the results of research related to recognizing emotions using anthropometric facial features. Emotions are recognized by estimating emotional arousal and emotional valence, in response to video material. Sixteen subjects participated in the experiment. Thirty four anthropometric features were extracted, based on the distances between the characteristic points on the face. The correlation of the developed arousal and valence estimators with the answers given in the questionnaires was 0.6 and 0.48.

articleTitle: Indirect Method for Kilovolt Nanosecond Pulses Measurement
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article presents the construction of a system that allows to measure the output voltage of a marx generator generating nanosecond pulses with a voltage amplitude of hundreds of kilovolts and low energy. The assumption of the structure was that the measuring system influence on the generator output would be as small as possible. To achieve this goal, it was decided to use an indirect measurement, based on the measurement of the electrical field in the reference electrode arrangement, with a small capacity and inductance. The article presents the results of tests and numerical analysis of the system.

articleTitle: A piezoelectric Foil Sensor used for Arterial Pulse Measurement
publicationTitle: 19th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering
abstract: The article deals with principle of the heart activity measurement using a piezoelectric sensor. There is an information about design of the device serving for arterial pulse wave measurement. The device allows conversion of an electrical charge from the piezoelectric sensor and offers analog signal preprocessing. The signal is later digital processed to achieve a heart rate of the measured subject.
